result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is a tree. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12835-L12936){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_tree() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is tree](/assets/graphs/is-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: six nodes connected with five edges and no cycle, so is_tree() returns True. Right: the same graph plus one extra edge between E and F, which closes the cycle A, B, E, F, C (shown in the accent color), so is_tree() returns False." width="100%"} A tree is a connected, acyclic, undirected graph. For a graph with *n* nodes to be a tree it: - must be undirected - must be connected (single component) - must have exactly *n - 1* edges - must be acyclic In practice the method checks the edge count and connectivity, which together guarantee acyclicity (see the notes below). A tree has exactly one path between any two nodes, which is why the property matters in applications such as: - validating hierarchies (org charts, taxonomies, file systems) stored as undirected graphs - confirming that a spanning-tree or network-design result has no redundant links - checking a precondition for algorithms that only work on trees Any self-loop or parallel edge creates a cycle, so a tree is always a simple graph. Directed graphs always return `False`, whatever their size; use `is_arborescence()` to test for a directed (rooted) tree. Undirected graphs with zero nodes, or one node and no self-loop, are treated as trees. The whole graph is checked and the current selection is ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graph is a tree, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The four conditions above are not independent: for a connected undirected graph on $n$ nodes, any two of "connected", "acyclic", and "has exactly $n - 1$ edges" imply the third, which is why definitions of a tree vary across textbooks yet describe the same object. Directed analogues live under `is_arborescence()`, and if you want to allow multiple disjoint components use `is_forest()` instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A connected, acyclic, undirected graph -- like this path -- qualifies as a tree: ::: {#1314029d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec tree = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) tree.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Closing the path into a cycle violates the "acyclic" requirement: ::: {#013a670e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cycle = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) cycle.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Leaving a node unconnected violates the "connected" requirement instead: ::: {#ac62cea9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} disconnected = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) # C is isolated -- no edge connects it .add_edge("A", "B") ) disconnected.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Generated structures like star graphs are trees too, since they're connected and have exactly `n - 1` edges: ::: {#735b4377 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} star = ec.Graph(directed=False) star.add_star_graph(n=5) star.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Direction disqualifies a graph, even when its shape is a tree. The same path built as a directed graph returns `False`, while `is_arborescence()` accepts it: ::: {#5cf035d1 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed_path = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=3) directed_path.is_tree(), directed_path.is_arborescence() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` (False, True) ``` ::: :::
